verses.english: Linked Discourses 4.10
1. Lifespan
Lifespan (2nd)
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
There the Buddha … said:
“Mendicants, the lifespan of humans is short.

verses.pali: Gamanīyo samparāyo, kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ, caritabbaṁ brahmacariyaṁ.
verses.english: You must go to the next life. So you should do what is skillful, you should practice the spiritual life.
No-one born is immortal.

verses.pali: Yo, bhikkhave, ciraṁ jīvati, so vassasataṁ appaṁ vā bhiyyo”ti.
verses.english: A long life is a hundred years or a little more.”

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“The days and nights don’t rush by,
and life isn’t cut short.
The life of mortals keeps rolling on,
like a chariot’s rim around the hub.”
“The days and nights rush by,
and then life is cut short.
The life of mortals wastes away,
like the water in tiny streams.”

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.
